messages:
alex: heads-up :wave: planning a phased maintenance in apac-west1 — kernel + NIC microcode roll, plus a minor driver bump. window: 2026-03-25 02:00-06:00 UTC. we'll do cohort drains (10% of GPU nodes per cohort), ~15m cordon + graceful evacuate each, aim for rolling reboots with warm cache. no full-region outage planned.

maria: noted. are Dedicated pools affected or only hosted?

alex: both pools in apac-west1 will see node-level drains. Dedicated tenants pinned to physical hosts will get planned handoffs to other racks if possible. Hosted will be routed to healthy pools/regions per smart routing policy.

jin: what's the canary plan? want to validate kernel+nic on 3 GPU nodes first before wide roll.

alex: yes — canary cohort of 3 nodes at start. if telemetry (p95 latency, error-rate) looks good for 20m, proceed. rollback path: immediate drain of cohort and mark firmware as blocked.

rachel: ops ask — please enable extra burst capacity during window. we can un-throttle burst pools and lift soft-eviction for preemptible backfill. also will increase autoscale headroom by 20%.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: auto-scheduled maintenance ticket created #MNT-4821, ETA 2026-03-25T02:00Z. Notifying customers with >1TB/day usage.

sam: cost note — increasing burst headroom will run extra GPUs reserved for ~4h, estimate ~$8k additional infra cost. is that approved?

maria: +1 to proceed, prefer stability over cost for this window. track spend and we'll reconcile.

alex: agreed. we'll attach cost labels to the autoscale actions so we can attribute.

jin: eviction strategy? prefer graceful preemption + reschedule to other zones where applicable. also add 5m KV-cache warmup after node comes back.

alex: plan: kubectl cordon + drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; ML tasks get SIGTERM with 2m grace by default, then force kill. We'll extend grace period for long-running inferences via the scheduler override for this window. snippet:

```
# drain example
kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-123
kubectl drain node/gpu-node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

rachel: also add canary traffic tag so we can route a tiny % (1%) of production requests to canary nodes for end-to-end validation.

alex: will do. telemetry hooks to watch: request p95, tail latency, token-per-second, model-fallback events. if model-fallbacks > 0.5% or p95 regresses >25% we abort.

ops-bot: incident-prep: on abort, automated rollback will mark firmware as blocked and trigger immediate headroom scale in other regions. Pager duty: infra-oncall -> primary -> secondary.

maria: customer comms draft posted in #announcements, pls review. short note about staggered maintenance and minimal impact, include contact for SRE during window.

jin: one more ask — please skip any nodes with hardware flagged as 'nvlink-unstable' in the last 30 days. don't want to mix firmware on flaky hw.

alex: good catch. I'll filter cohort selection by health tags.

rachel: final checklist: canary +20m, metrics OK, burst headroom live, customer comms sent, ops runbook synced. anyone blocking?

sam: no blockers from finance.

maria: no blockers from product.

alex: thanks. will post minute-by-minute updates in this thread during the window. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
